subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: What are the products of a neutralisation reaction between an acid and a base?
questions.explain: Acid + base → salt + water is the general neutralisation reaction.

questions.q: What is the pH of a neutral solution such as pure water?
questions.explain: A neutral solution has a pH of exactly 7 on the 0–14 scale.

questions.q: In a titration, how do you know the exact end point of the neutralisation?
questions.explain: A suitable indicator changes colour at the end point, showing neutralisation is complete.

questions.q: When making copper sulfate crystals from copper oxide and sulfuric acid, how is the excess copper oxide removed?
questions.explain: The unreacted solid copper oxide is filtered off, leaving the copper sulfate solution.

questions.q: Which salt is formed when hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydroxide?
questions.explain: Hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts, so sodium chloride is formed.

questions.q: A substance that does not move from the baseline in chromatography is most likely:
questions.explain: A spot that stays on the baseline is insoluble in that solvent and does not travel.

questions.q: When sodium hydroxide is added to a solution of copper(II) ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Copper(II) ions form a blue precipitate of copper hydroxide with sodium hydroxide.

questions.q: In a flame test, lithium ions give which colour?
questions.explain: Lithium ions produce a crimson flame.

questions.q: Chlorine gas is identified because it:
questions.explain: Chlorine bleaches damp litmus paper, turning it white.

questions.q: Which gas turns limewater milky, confirming it is given off when acid reacts with a carbonate?
questions.explain: Carbon dioxide turns limewater milky, confirming the gas from acid + carbonate reactions.

questions.q: Which acid is used to make a sulfate salt?
questions.explain: Sulfuric acid produces sulfate salts.

questions.q: What colour does universal indicator turn in a strongly acidic solution?
questions.explain: Universal indicator turns red in strongly acidic conditions (low pH).

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a solution containing iodide ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Iodide ions form a yellow precipitate of silver iodide.

questions.q: What is produced when an acid reacts with a metal oxide?
questions.explain: A metal oxide is a base, so acid + metal oxide → salt + water.

questions.q: A weak acid and a strong acid have the same pH. Which statement is true?
options: The weak acid is more concentrated
The strong acid is more concentrated
questions.explain: Because a weak acid only partially ionises, it needs a higher concentration to reach the same pH.

questions.q: How can you test for the presence of carbonate ions?
options: Add acid and bubble the gas through limewater
Add silver nitrate to form a precipitate
questions.explain: Carbonates react with acid to release carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

questions.q: In chemistry, a formulation is best described as:
options: A useful mixture made in carefully measured quantities
questions.explain: A formulation is a mixture made to a precise recipe, such as paint or a medicine.

questions.q: In a titration, which piece of apparatus delivers a precisely measured, fixed volume of one solution?
questions.explain: A pipette is used to measure an accurate fixed volume, while the burette delivers a variable volume.

questions.q: What gas is given off when a reactive metal reacts with a dilute acid?
questions.explain: Acid + metal → salt + hydrogen, so hydrogen gas is released.

questions.q: An alkali is best described as:
options: A metal that reacts with acid
A soluble base that releases OH- ions in water
questions.explain: An alkali is a soluble base that produces hydroxide (OH-) ions in aqueous solution.

questions.q: To test for halide ions with silver nitrate, why is dilute nitric acid added first?
options: To remove carbonate ions that would also give a precipitate
To make the gas test work
questions.explain: Nitric acid removes carbonate ions so they don't form a precipitate and give a false halide result.

questions.q: What is the difference between a strong acid and a weak acid?
options: Weak acids have a pH above 7
Strong acids fully ionise in water, weak acids only partially ionise
questions.explain: Strength refers to the degree of ionisation: strong acids ionise completely, weak acids only partially.
